q: All are signs of an upper motor neurone lesion EXCEPT:
e: Fasciculation is a lower motor neurone sign.

q: The ankle reflex is supplied mainly by:
e: Ankle reflex S1; knee reflex L3–L4.

q: A 4-year-old boy climbs up his legs to stand and has big calves. The first test is:
e: Gowers' sign with calf pseudohypertrophy suggests Duchenne dystrophy: CK is very high.

q: A child born at 29 weeks has stiff legs with scissoring and nearly normal arms. The type of CP is:
e: Preterm babies get periventricular leukomalacia, which causes spastic diplegia.

q: Which finding argues AGAINST cerebral palsy?
e: CP is non-progressive; regression suggests a degenerative disease.

q: Writhing involuntary movements after severe neonatal jaundice indicate:
e: Kernicterus damages the basal ganglia, causing dyskinetic CP.

q: An infant has a large head, bulging fontanelle, separated sutures and sunsetting eyes. The best first imaging is:
e: With an open fontanelle, cranial ultrasound shows dilated ventricles without radiation.

q: All are signs of rickets EXCEPT:
e: Koplik spots are a sign of measles.

q: The heart lesion most typical of Down syndrome is:
e: AVSD (and VSD) are the typical lesions in Down syndrome.
